slot.brief: Circuit with ideal diodes in series/parallel with resistors; determine which diodes conduct and compute the current through a specified branch.

verdicts.working: Battery drives current from J1 to J2. D1 (pointing J1→J2) is forward biased; D2 (pointing J2→J1) is reverse biased and blocks its 12 Ω branch. Active parallel combination: 6 Ω || 12 Ω = 4 Ω, in series with 2 Ω gives 6 Ω. Total current = 18/6 = 3 A; voltage across J1–J2 = 3×4 = 12 V; current through D1 = 12/6 = 2.0 A.

working:
1. Determine the biasing of each diode:
The positive terminal of the $18\ \text{V}$ battery is connected to the left junction $J_1$, and the negative terminal connects via the $2\ \Omega$ resistor to the right junction $J_2$. Thus, $V_{J_1} > V_{J_2}$.
- Diode $D_1$ has its anode connected toward $J_1$ and cathode toward $J_2$, so it is forward-biased and acts as a closed switch.
- Diode $D_2$ has its cathode connected toward $J_1$ and anode toward $J_2$, so it is reverse-biased and acts as an open circuit ($I_{D_2} = 0$).

2. Find the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination:
Only the top branch ($6\ \Omega$) and the bottom branch ($12\ \Omega$) conduct.
$$R_p = \dfrac{6 \times 12}{6 + 12} = 4\ \Omega$$

3. Calculate the total circuit resistance and total current:
$$R_{\text{total}} = R_p + 2\ \Omega = 4 + 2 = 6\ \Omega$$
$$I_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{18\ \text{V}}{6\ \Omega} = 3\ \text{A}$$

4. Calculate the current through diode $D_1$:
The voltage drop across the parallel section is:
$$V_p = I_{\text{total}} \times R_p = 3\ \text{A} \times 4\ \Omega = 12\ \text{V}$$
Therefore, the current through $D_1$ is:
$$I_{D_1} = \dfrac{V_p}{6\ \Omega} = \dfrac{12\ \text{V}}{6\ \Omega} = 2.0\ \text{A}$$

figure.description: A rectangular schematic circuit. On the left vertical branch is a DC voltage source labeled '18 V' with its positive terminal (longer line) at the top and negative terminal (shorter line) at the bottom. From the positive terminal, the wire runs horizontally right to a node J1. Between node J1 and a second node J2, three horizontal branches are connected in parallel: (1) Top branch: an ideal diode D1 pointing to the right (anode to J1, cathode to J2) in series with a 6 Ω resistor. (2) Middle branch: an ideal diode D2 pointing to the left (cathode to J1, anode to J2) in series with a 12 Ω resistor. (3) Bottom branch: a simple 12 Ω resistor with no diode. From node J2, the circuit wire continues to the right, turns downward, and returns horizontally to the negative terminal of the battery through a resistor labeled '2 Ω'.
